title: Trump intel chief warned no funding for Musk’s SpaceX without answers on Ukraine Starshield slowdown | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

A top Congressional Democrat is warning that lawmakers will withhold government funding for systems developed by Elon Musk’s SpaceX if the Trump administration and tech billionaire refuse to disclose who is responsible for ordering the slowdown of Ukraine’s military-grade Starlink satellite service, CNN has learned.

In a classified communication sent to Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, Democratic Rep. Jim Himes — who will become chairman of the House Intelligence Committee in January — demanded clarity on what led to theslowdown of Ukraine’s Starshield connection speedon multiple occasions in recent months, according to an excerpt of the communication obtained by CNN.

“Simply, our committee cannot authorize funds for the development of government systems that the government will not fully control,” Himes wrote to Clayton. “I appreciate your assistance in obtaining transparency in this instance so we can have confidence going forward in authorizing funding for the development of systems using SpaceX as the primary vendor.”

The warning comes as a growing number of Democrats have vowed to investigate the limits on Ukraine’s Starshield system, which Ukraine relies on for its defenses. After two rounds of days-long speed restrictions, there has been little clarity on who is responsible. Democratic lawmakers in both the House and Senate have said they plan to scrutinize the Trump administration’s broader dealings with Russia when the party takes control of Congress in January.

Himes’ determination to investigation the slowdown comes as Zelensky has said in recent days that the Starshield system is facing limits once again, while Ukraine is facing massive renewed attacks from Russia even after Trump met with Putin earlier this week.

Himes has also formally requested a meeting with Musk to discuss the slowdown, according toa separate lettersent to the SpaceX CEO obtained by CNN.

“My ask to you is straightforward. Explain the changes that were made to the Starshield service in October 2026, why those changes were made and whether those changes were made unilaterally by SpaceX or were directed by a US government official,” Himes wrote to Musk.

“My view, which I have conveyed to senior Administration officials, is that SpaceX’s potentially unilateral modification of a US government contract, combined with its lack of responsiveness to congressional oversight, calls into question every contract the US government has with SpaceX, including the development of what you describe as the separate military-grade ‘systems owned and controlled by the US government,’” the letter to Musk states.

CNN has reached out to SpaceX for comment.

When Himes becomes chairman of the House Intelligence Committee in January, one of his top priorities will be investigating Musk’s control over SpaceX systems like Starshield and, if needed, leverage the power of the purse to extract answers from the company about the slowdown, according to a source familiar with his thinking.

The most obvious tool at Himes’ disposal for doing so is known as “ring fencing,” which allows the committee to legally restrict funding for certain projects in the annual Intelligence Authorization Act until certain conditions are met.

Himes could also work with congressional appropriators to redirect or block additional funding for SpaceX systems if the company and Trump administration continue to stonewall lawmakers.

According to Himes, the classified message to Clayton and the public letter sent to SpaceX raise two primary concerns: a lack of clarity around who made decisions that impeded Ukraine’s defense, and the lack of responsiveness from relevant government entities, as well as SpaceX, to questions from lawmakers to date.

The limitations were in place for several weeks in October. Earlier this month, Zelensky said that renewed limitations were in effect over the occupied territories of Ukraine. Those restrictions have now been in place for more than a week. Denys Sienik, Ukraine’s top diplomat in the US, told CNN Friday that they are in touch with the Pentagon but have received no response from SpaceX.

SpaceX maintains billions of dollars in US government contracts for space-based systems, occupying a uniquely critical role in national security as a result. Those contracts are a source of leverage for lawmakers but following through on any threat to restrict funding for SpaceX systems carries the risk of compromising irreplaceable assets the US relies on for its own national defense.

The Trump administration, Musk and SpaceX executives have offered various accounts of who authorized the throttling of Ukraine’s Starshield connection speed, a move that led to the disruption of its military internet service and slowed down a critical system for launching missile and drone attacks, as well as defending against Russian strikes.

The initial issues with Starshield were discovered in mid-October after the Trump administration threatened to withhold intelligence to Kyiv over its strikes on Russian refineries and after Trump made a deal to buy Russian diesel and ease sanctions on Moscow. The US president had sparred with President Volodymyr Zelensky and suggested Ukraine should get a new leader.

Reports about that slowdown in the Starlink service led to confusion inside the White House, where many officials were initially unsure what, if any, role the US government had played.

The Senate Foreign Relations Committee is also planning to investigate the Starshield slowdown once Democrats assume the majority in Congress, CNN previously reported. Last week, the outgoing top Democrat and incoming chair of the committee sent a letter to Musk demanding that he and SpaceX preserve documents related to the disruptions.

While Trump advisers were aware of his frustrations with Zelensky before he lashed out publicly, they had not heard the president discuss specific plans to hamper Kyiv’s ability to strike Russian diesel refineries, which he has blamed on rising global energy prices.

Trump told officials he wanted to find out where the slowdown originated and would later tell reporters he wasn’t personally involved in the decision. Officials inside the administration understood that as a directive to investigate the matter and look into how the system was slowed down.

Privately, SpaceX executives and defense officials have told some inquiring lawmakers that the decision to initiate the slowdown in October originally came from the White House, a source familiar with those discussions told CNN, though Trump has repeatedly denied any direct involvement.

Ultimately, top Trump officials appeared to put responsibility on the privately owned SpaceX and its “terms of service” with Ukraine.

The exact nature of those terms of service as they relate to Ukraine’s ability to use Starshield are largely classified, according to a source familiar with the matter.

But there are conditions and caveats for allies like Ukraine to share the capability, meaning Ukraine’s use of Starshield is “very dependent upon the US saying yes” with specific contract clauses that allow them to do it, the source added.

The Pentagon’s arrangement with SpaceX for Starshield is complicated by the “Elon factor,” the source acknowledged, pointing to Musk’s unique level of authority at the company allowing him to dictate program changes from the top down.

But Starshield is still a government-managed application, the source added.

“SpaceX flies it on behalf of the of the U.S. government, but the U.S. government is completely in control of how it gets tasked, how it gets used, who gets access to it,” they said.

“Starshield is a Pentagon system,” one of the sources, a US official, also reiterated, drawing a distinction between SpaceX’s role in managing the military-grade satellite system compared to how the company operates its commercially available version, known as Starlink.

Yet a Pentagon official told CNN that Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth had no involvement or foreknowledge of the slowdown – raising further questions about who was ultimately responsible.

“He had no idea it was happening,” the official said, referring to Hegseth.

In the immediate aftermath of the slowdown, some Trump officials began pointing the finger at Musk, saying he “went rogue” and acted unilaterally. Trump made no such request to throttle Starshield, one senior US official told CNN at the time.

“Elon did it unilaterally,” another US official previously insisted.

Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle have raised concerns about the prospect of Musk using his seemingly unprecedented powers over government-managed systems, like Starshield, to unilaterally enact foreign policy on behalf of the US.

Both Democratic and Republican lawmakers had called for a Pentagon watchdog investigation into the slowdown and whether it, in combination with issues in early missile warnings, put American personnel at risk. But that request was declined by the Pentagon Inspector General who instructed lawmakers to direct their questions to the relevant military service branches.

“There is an outcome where it was actually really bad activity and contravention of a Pentagon contract or maybe (SpaceX) did something they were entitled to do but just did not give anybody any warning,” Himes told CNN in an interview this week.

“But we are going to get to the bottom of it. There is a lot at stake here,” he added.

In his letter to Musk, Himes stresses that the authorization of US government funding for all SpaceX systems is at risk if the tech billionaire refuses to provide answers.

“It is difficult for me to continue supporting the authorization of funding for these SpaceX-developed, government-owned systems, until I receive satisfactory answers to my questions about the Starshield service in Ukraine,” he wrote to Musk.
